newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile Jan supermarket sales up vs '96, Feb down.
newsitem.headline: Chile Jan supermarket sales up vs '96, Feb down.

text.p: Chilean supermarket sales grew 4.3 percent in January on the same month last year but fell 1.7 percent in February, said the Chilean Association of Supermarkets.
The figures showed supermarket sales growing 1.4 percent in the first two months on the year, much lower than the 9.6 percent growth recorded in the same period of 1996, said the statement.
The slowdown is a result of the Central Bank's high interest rate policy, which has put a brake on consumer spending since mid-1996.
"The signals indicate that this trend should break from the second half of the year, with sales in the third quarter recovering to levels seen in the first half of 1996," said the association.
Chileans are among Latin America's most enthusiastic supermarket shoppers and supermarket sales are widely regarded as a barometer of consumer spending.
